source: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF), General Directorate of Agriculture, Department of Agricultural Extension — 'បច្ចេកទេសដាំដំណាំឪឡឹក' (Watermelon Cultivation Techniques), 2017.
text:
Watermelon is generally ready for harvest about 50 to 60 days after planting, though the exact timing depends on the variety grown. Farmers judge ripeness using several signs: the small curling tendril near the fruit's stem dries up and turns brown/yellow; the fruit's skin develops its full, correct color pattern and stripe markings for the variety; and the patch of rind where the fruit rests on the ground (or on the mulch) changes from white/pale to a yellowish color. Fruit should not be picked before it shows these signs, since harvesting too early reduces fruit quality (sweetness and ripeness).

At harvest, a knife or cutting tool should be used to cut the fruit from the vine carefully, rather than pulling or twisting it off, to avoid damaging the remaining vine and any developing fruit nearby. According to the source, from planting through to harvest, watermelon grown following these techniques can produce an average yield of about 15 to 17 tons per hectare.
